The public RAWGraphs app is a React GUI around those two libraries. The
GifOS copy keeps the load → choose a visual model → map columns → draw SVG
loop and a working set of those models (alluvial, treemap, bar, stacked bar,
line, bubble, pie, bump, beeswarm, sunburst, circle packing, streamgraph).
The React shell, the Excel importer, and charts that pull extra d3 plugins
(hexbin, voronoi-treemap, chord, contour) are not shipped: the sandbox has
no eval and no network, and lodash/d3 UMD builds call Function() at load.

Chart renders here follow the same visual-variable names (bars, steps,
hierarchy, size, series) so a mapping from the original still makes sense.
The last CSV and the last mapping are saved privately. Upstream has no save.
